articles.title: La Chine réalise l'impossible : elle crée une batterie au lithium innovante capable de maintenir son autonomie, même à −50 °C
articles.text:
La Chine réalise l'impossible : elle crée une batterie au lithium innovante capable de maintenir son autonomie, même à −50 °C
Des chercheurs de l'Université de Nankai ont dévoilé une batterie au lithium qui fonctionne encore par −70 °C et stocke deux fois plus d'énergie que les modèles actuels. Le secret : un électrolyte qui rompt avec un siècle de chimie. La découverte est spectaculaire, mais encore loin de nos voitures.
Tout conducteur de voiture électrique connaît la mauvaise surprise de l'hiver. Un matin de gel, l'autonomie affichée fond de 20, parfois 40 %, et la recharge s'éternise. Ce n'est pas un défaut de fabrication, mais une limite physique que l'on croyait presque indépassable : le froid paralyse la chimie interne des batteries. C'est précisément ce verrou, vieux comme la batterie elle-même, qu'une équipe chinoise affirme avoir fait sauter.
Pourquoi le froid tue les batteries
Pour comprendre l'exploit, il faut regarder ce qui se passe àl'intérieur d'une batterie quand le thermomètre chute. Le cœur du système, c'est l'électrolyte, ce liquide dans lequel voyagent les ions lithium d'un bout à l'autre de la cellule à chaque charge et décharge. Dans toutes les batteries actuelles, ce liquide repose sur des solvants à base d'oxygène, un choix hérité des débuts de la chimie des piles.
Le problème, c'est que ces solvants s'accrochent trop fort à l'ion lithium. Pour circuler, l'ion doit sans cesse se libérer de cette étreinte. Or cette opération demande de l'énergie. Par grand froid, cette énergie manque, l'ion peine à se détacher, le courant ralentit et les performances s'effondrent. C'est la fameuse barrière de désolvatation, le mur invisible contre lequel butent les batteries en hiver. L'équipe de Nankai a eu une idée radicale : remplacer l'oxygène par le fluor.
Le pari du fluor, une rupture de fond
En troquant les solvants oxygénés pour une molécule fluorée, le 1,3-difluoropropane, les chercheurs ont volontairement affaibli le lien entre le solvant et le lithium. L'ion, moins retenu, se libère beaucoup plus facilement, même dans un froid glacial. C'est un renversement de logique : là où la chimie classique cherchait des liaisons solides, cette approche mise sur une accroche délibérément lâche pour fluidifier la circulation.
Les résultats mesurés en laboratoire sont impressionnants. La batterie atteint 707 wattheures par kilo à température ambiante, soit plus du double des meilleures batteries lithium-ion du commerce, qui plafonnent autour de 250 à 300. Surtout, elle conserve environ 400 wattheures par kilo à −50 °C, et continue de fonctionner jusqu'à −70 °C, une température qu'aucune batterie classique ne supporte. À ce niveau de froid, elle restitue encore l'essentiel de son courant avec une efficacité de 98 %. Sur le papier, c'est la fin de la double malédiction des batteries : il fallait jusqu'ici choisir entre densité d'énergie et résistance au froid, ce système promet les deux.
De l'exploit scientifique à la route, un long chemin
Faut-il pour autant s'attendre à faire le plein de kilomètres cet hiver ? Certainement pas, et c'est là qu'il faut raison garder face aux titres enthousiastes. Ces performances ont été obtenues sur de petites cellules de laboratoire, pas dans un véhicule. Or, entre la prouesse en éprouvette et la batterie industrielle, les obstacles sont nombreux et sérieux. Le plus criant : la durée de vie. À ce stade, la batterie ne tient qu'environ 115 cycles de charge, quand l'automobile en exige plusieurs milliers. Elle s'userait donc en quelques mois.
D'autres défis restent entiers. Le solvant fluoré est volatil, il s'évapore dès 48 °C, ce qui pose des problèmes de sécurité et de stabilité par temps chaud, un comble pour une technologie du froid. Les chercheurs planchent déjà sur des molécules plus lourdes pour y remédier. S'ajoutent le risque de dendrites, ces filaments de lithium qui peuvent provoquer un court-circuit sur le long terme, et un coût de fabrication supérieur aux électrolytes classiques. Cette batterie ne roulera donc pas demain dans nos rues. Mais en brisant un dogme chimique vieux de deux siècles, elle ouvre une piste précieuse, d'abord pour l'aérospatiale, les drones de haute altitude ou les missions polaires, là où le froid extrême est la règle et où chaque gramme compte. La révolution n'est pas pour tout de suite, l'avancée scientifique, elle, est bien réelle.

articles.title: Obama urges Democrats to have a ‘clear plan’ for AI safeguards | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Former President Barack Obama recently said that Democrats need to make artificial intelligence one of their “central agendas” and “have a very clear plan” to address concerns around the technology’s economic impact and safety, according to The New York Times.
Obama made these comments on Thursday, at Democratic fundraising event where he was interviewed by House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries. The NYT says that Obama’s office provided a partial transcript of the event, at which Jeffries asked Obama how congressional Democrats should approach AI.
In response, Obama said that once Democrats regain the House majority, they need to “put together a framework for a very public conversation.”
“This is something that is moving very fast in private hands, and if we don’t get on top of it, I think can be dangerous,” Obama added. “If we do get on top of it, I do think it’s beneficial. I genuinely think it’s going to accelerate, for example, drug development in ways that can help us cure diseases.”
In a statement, Jeffries said the former president “is correct that decisive action must be taken on artificial intelligence.” Jeffries also said that “Republicans have abdicated their responsibility to govern on behalf of the American people.”
The NYT also reports that Obama has offered himself as a “sounding board” to AI executives and has spoken to both Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. His comments come amidst growing concern around AI safety, particularly after an AI researcher resigned from Anthropic and claimed the leading AI companies are “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.”
On Saturday, Amodei outlined a broad approach to “pacing the frontier,” which would include giving independent safety evaluators access to leading AI companies and models, as well as developing “common safety standards” between companies. In social media posts, Altman and SpaceX CEO Musk seemed to respond positively to Amodei’s plan, with Altman saying that OpenAI would also commit to “having independent evaluators with employee-like access.”
President Donald Trump, meanwhile, discussed AI safety concerns with reporters at an Irish golf event on Sunday. Bloomberg reports that Trump boasted that the United States is “the most sophisticated country in the world,” adding that he wants “to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins.” (Earlier this year, the Trump administration released a legislative framework for AI that would preempt state laws and shift the child safety burden to parents.)
“And we can put guardrails,” Trump said. “We can do this and that. But I think you have a lot of negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn’t be bringing it up.”

articles.title: Thrustmaster Airbus Add-On Grip with AVA Joystick Base Review: A First-Class Flight Experience
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Thrustmaster AVA Base paired with the Airbus Add-On Grip delivers almost everything we expect from a high-end flight stick, but the wobble in its standard configuration is unfortunate and requires dampers to fix, and its high cost may put it out of reach for many people.
Pros
- +Very similar ergonomically to the real Airbus sidestick
- +Very precise
- +No center detent
- +Progressive resistance
Cons
- -Stick wobbles due to lack of damping out of the box
- -Pricing
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
The past few years have been an exciting time for flight simulation hardware. Established brands and newcomers alike have introduced a wide range of new products, making it easier and more affordable than ever to build a capable home cockpit.
Thrustmaster has long been one of the leading names in flight simulation hardware. Its HOTAS Warthog has been a staple in home cockpits since its release, earning a reputation for its robust construction. In 2024, Thrustmaster introduced the AVA Joystick Base, bringing several notable improvements over the Warthog base. Until recently, however, there wasn't a dedicated Airbus grip compatible with the AVA base.
In this review, we'll be taking a look at the recently released Thrustmaster Airbus Add-On Grip paired with the AVA Joystick Base. We will put both the grip and the base to the test using the Fenix A320 in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024.
Inside the Box
The Airbus Add-on Grip contains the grip itself, the A400M module, and a button cover.
The AVA Base contains the joystick base, two sets of two cams (Aero and Jet), three sets of two springs (Soft, Medium, and Strong), three masks (Small, Medium, and XL), two Allen keys, and one detachable USB-C cable.
- Airbus Add-on Grip Dimensions: 3.1 inches / 78 mm wide, 3.3 inches / 83 mm deep, 7.7 inches / 195 mm tall. Weight: 0.4 lb / 203 g.
- AVA Base Dimensions: 4.3 inches / 108 mm wide, 6.7 inches / 170 mm deep, 2.8 inches / 72 mm tall. Weight: 2.4 lb / 1,069 g.
Thrustmaster also sent us an AVA Base Plate for easier desktop mounting, along with AVA Dual Pitch Cam. The Dual Pitch Cam contains two FBW (fly-by-wire) cams which are meant to simulate the sensation of a fly-by-wire aircraft.
All of these products are sold separately.

| Dimensions (LxWxH)  | 4.3 x 6.7 x 2.8 inches / 108 x 170 x 72 mm  | 
| Weight  | 2.4lbs / 1,069g  | 
| MSRP  | $299.99  | 
| Release Date  | May 2024  | 
Customization
One of the primary goals of the AVA Base is to provide a high degree of customization, allowing users to tailor the joystick to their preferred flying experience. The interchangeable cams let you adjust the axis curve, different springs allow you to fine-tune resistance, and the various deflection masks can be used to limit the range of travel.
The user manual includes recommended configurations for different types of aircraft. Since we’re testing the Airbus Add-On Grip, we’ll configure the AVA Base for an airliner-style feel. According to the manual, this involves using the Jet Cam with the Medium spring. However, as mentioned earlier, Thrustmaster also provided us with a pair of FBW cams that are designed to deliver an even more authentic experience by simulating the control feel of a fly-by-wire aircraft, such as those in the Airbus A3XX family.
The AVA Base also comes with T.A.R.G.E.T (Thrustmaster Advanced pRogramming Graphical EdiTor), which is an application that allows you to further tune the feel of the axes and access advanced profiles created by the Thrustmaster community.
Like the AVA Base, the Airbus Add-On Grip also offers several customization options. For example, it includes a module and button cover that transform the grip from an A3XX sidestick into an A400M sidestick. Additionally, the Z-axis can be locked out using an integrated mechanical lock, preventing unintended twist inputs.
Overall, customizing the base and the grip was very straightforward.
Build Quality
The AVA Base has a premium feel, with a high-quality plastic outer shell complemented by a metal top plate. The are only two drawbacks. On its own, the base is not stable enough to handle larger stick inputs. We therefore recommend pairing it with the optional AVA Base Plate, which significantly improves stability. Additionally, the base does not include enough damping out of the box, causing the stick to wobble if you move it with a finger. This is not noticeable during normal flight, but stronger damping would have been a welcome inclusion. Thrustmaster offers additional dampers, which are sold separately, that address this issue.
The Airbus Add-On Grip is designed as a 1:1 replica of the Airbus A3XX sidestick, closely matching the shape and ergonomics of its real-world counterpart. In its standard airliner configuration, it features the signature red autopilot disconnect button. It also includes an interchangeable module and removable button cover, allowing it to be converted into an A400M-style sidestick.
Both the AVA Base and Airbus Add-On Grip use Hall effect sensors with 16-bit precision. The base employs them on the X and Y axes, while the grip uses them for the twist (Z) axis and integrated mini-stick.
How Does it Feel?
The first thing that stood out was how much more authentic the AVA Base felt compared to the Thrustmaster Warthog. Unlike the Warthog, there is no noticeable center detent as you pass through the neutral position. Resistance increases progressively as the stick moves farther from center, resulting in smoother and more natural control inputs.
Compared to the Thrustmaster TCA Airbus Sidestick, the AVA Base also has less overall travel on both the X and Y axes, with a progressively increasing resistance rather than the TCA's more linear feel. Based on previous experience with an A320 simulator, this behavior closely matches the feel of the real Airbus sidestick, making the controls feel more authentic.
The Hall effect technology and 16-bit precision of the AVA Base also allow the user to make very fine and precise inputs. In normal conditions, that is exactly how one would fly an Airbus - using small, deliberate sidestick movements.
The Airbus Add-On Grip captures the look and feel of the real Airbus sidestick, with ergonomics that make it feel instantly familiar to anyone who has flown or used an Airbus simulator.
Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 Testing
We tested the AVA Base and Airbus Add-On Grip in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 using the Fenix A320. While there are several Airbus aircraft available for MSFS 2024, we chose the Fenix because it offers one of the most accurate flight models and flight dynamics for an Airbus plane in the sim, making it the best platform for evaluating Airbus flight controls.
We also tested with a pair of FBW cams designed to replicate the feel of an Airbus fly-by-wire sidestick. However, based on our experience with an A320 simulator, we found that the standard Jet cams included with the AVA Base felt more authentic. The FBW cams introduced a more noticeable center detent, whereas the Jet cams provided a smoother transition through center, more closely matching the feel of a real Airbus sidestick.
We tested the base and stick in three difference scenarios:
- Basic maneuvering. Flying at 5,000 feet, we performed gentle turns and pitch changes to evaluate the precision of the base during small, accurate control inputs.
- Turbulent approach. We performed an approach into Las Vegas under hot, windy conditions with strong updrafts and downdrafts. This scenario required larger, more frequent control inputs to assess the resistance and how the base handles turbulence and rapid corrections.
- Curved approach. Finally, we flew the RNAV Visual approach to Runway 1R at San Francisco International Airport. This approach is available in MSFS 2024 if you use the Navigraph database, but it is missing the RF leg between the waypoints KLAUS and SQIRL, so we added it to the navigation database of the Fenix A320 ourselves. The procedure features a sweeping right-hand arc that continues until roughly one mile from the runway threshold, requiring the aircraft to remain in a turn at very low altitude. The approach demands precise tracking of the flight path while also requiring a smooth, accurate transition to the runway centerline after the final waypoint. This scenario tested both the precision and responsiveness of the AVA Base.
Basic Maneuvering
While flying at 5,000 feet, we were impressed by the AVA Base’s precision when making small adjustments to both pitch and roll. Compared to the Warthog and TCA Airbus Sidestick, the AVA Base allowed for significantly finer roll inputs, making it easier to make small corrections and maintain a precise flight path.
When controlling vertical speed through pitch adjustments, we were able to consistently achieve the desired climb or descent rate within approximately 100 feet per minute, demonstrating the level of control possible with the high-resolution sensors.
Turbulent Approach
Landing in Las Vegas during the summer can be a challenging experience. The combination of extreme heat, strong winds, and thermals along the approach path can create significant turbulence, resulting in a much less stable approach. Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is able to replicate these conditions through its Live Weather system. While it is important to avoid overcorrecting and creating pilot-induced oscillations, these conditions require more frequent and sometimes larger control inputs than a typical approach.
The AVA Base handled this turbulent approach very well. The conditions forced us to make slightly larger inputs, so we felt the progressive resistance of the base as we moved further from center, which felt authentic. We were also able to make very quick corrections to counter the turbulence and keep the aircraft on the published approach path.
Curved Approach
During the RNAV Visual approach to Runway 1R at San Francisco International Airport, we were able to precisely track the sweeping right-hand arc all the way to the final waypoint, SQIRL. Once established at SQIRL, the AVA Base’s responsiveness allowed us to smoothly align with the runway centerline.
Other products, including the Warthog and TCA Airbus Sidestick, produced more noticeable jerky movements during this approach, which is likely due to lower precision around the neutral position.
Overall Thoughts
After putting the AVA Base and Airbus Add-On Grip through extensive testing, we came away extremely impressed with the experience. As competitors have continued to close the gap with Thrustmaster Warthog — and even surpass it — the AVA Base represents a return to the level of quality and refinement we have come to expect from the brand.
The AVA Base delivered exceptional precision, smooth control, and an authentic Airbus-like feel across a variety of challenging flight scenarios. The addition of the recently released Airbus Add-On Grip finally allows users to pair this high-end base with a dedicated airline-style sidestick, making it a compelling option for anyone who regularly flies Airbus aircraft.
The biggest obstacle is the price. The level of engineering and build quality comes at a premium, which may put the AVA Base and Airbus Add-On Grip out of reach for many users. However, for those looking for a high-quality Airbus stick and willing to invest in a premium setup, the Thrustmaster AVA Base paired with the Airbus Add-On Grip is a compelling option.
Dan Mateescu is a PC enthusiast with many years of experience benchmarking PC hardware. In 2021, he started his own YouTube channel called 'Compusemble' where he benchmarks hardware in video games and the latest tech demos.

articles.title: Windows 11 September Update Kills Audio Output on Some PCs
articles.text:
Sunday, September 13th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Windows 11 September Update Kills Audio Output on Some PCs
Windows 11 continues its streak of breaking things, as Microsoft has confirmed that there is an issue with the latest September security update. According to the updated support document, Microsoft confirmed that the KB5124008 Windows security update can break audio output on some PCs. Specifically, this security update introduces issues with USB audio devices, where users of these audio output devices can't get any output from them. Messages include "This device cannot start (Code 10)" in the device manager, which fails to recognize some devices, while other symptoms can include unresponsive volume controls, no volume at all, no audio output, unresponsive sound settings, or the complete lack of detection in the device manager.
Microsoft confirmed that this only affects USB Audio Class 1.0 devices, but the current workaround is quite strange. Some USB audio devices can continue to function in standard stereo configuration. However, when switching to multichannel audio features such as 8-channel or 3D audio mode, the device can fail. The company is stating that the mileage will vary depending on the device type and use case, as some users were able to restore audio functions by switching to 2-channel audio mode in cases like these. However, do note that it doesn't mean that the problem is solved, but that only a few devices can find a workaround until a temporary fix is in place. Microsoft is reportedly working on a resolution.Interestingly, this is not the first case of strange bugs as Microsoft has already dealt with external devices that either break the OS or simply stop working after an OS update. Notably, a recent example is the Windows 11 August update, which reset custom cursors to an oversized default one. In some cases, the color and size settings don't stick, no matter how many times they are changed. This update has also caused gameplay issues, such as forced crashes, random freezing, errors, and unexpected device restarts due to RGB peripherals. We ran a poll of nearly 33,000 responses, with the majority of respondents stating that Windows 11 is degrading in quality of use, even after Microsoft's many promises. Hence, the streak of bad updates continues to this day.

articles.title: Sam Altman confirma que OpenAI no saldrá a bolsa en 2026 debido a las preocupaciones por la IA
articles.text:
Sam Altman, director ejecutivo de OpenAI, confirmó que la compañía no realizará su oferta pública inicial (IPO) en 2026. En una entrevista con la revista Fortune, el ejecutivo señaló que el clima actual en torno a la seguridad de la inteligencia artificial vuelve inoportuno cualquier movimiento hacia los mercados bursátiles.
“Creo que, dado todo lo que está sucediendo con la seguridad, este sería un momento poco recomendable para salir a bolsa, y no sentimos presión al respecto”, dijo Altman. El directivo añadió que OpenAI cotizará en bolsa cuando el negocio esté preparado y cuando la compañía considere adecuado el momento social en relación con la tecnología.
PUBLICIDAD
Consultado sobre si 2026 queda descartado en favor de 2027, Altman respondió: “Diría que no en 2026. Sí, tenemos mucho trabajo por delante, como atender lo que este momento va a requerir en materia de seguridad y alineación, y cómo la industria y los gobiernos pueden colaborar”.
Un giro respecto a los planes conocidos en junio
En junio, The New York Times había informado que OpenAI se inclinaba por postergar su salida a bolsa, una operación que podría valuar a la empresa en un billón de dólares. Uno de los factores considerados entonces fue la IPO de SpaceX, que recaudó 85.000 millones de dólares para la compañía aeroespacial y de inteligencia artificial de Elon Musk. Las acciones de esa firma subieron en un primer momento, lo que llevó su valuación a 1,8 billones de dólares, para luego caer con rapidez.
PUBLICIDAD
Los mercados globales atravesaban además un período de volatilidad, que continúa en la actualidad debido a la reescalada del conflicto en Irán, que volvió a impulsar los precios del petróleo y elevó las proyecciones de inflación.
Incidentes de seguridad alimentan la cautela
Las declaraciones de Altman se producen en medio de una creciente preocupación por la seguridad de la inteligencia artificial, tras una serie de episodios en los que enjambres de agentes de IA autónomos vulneraron sitios como Hugging Face y se comunicaron entre sí de manera encubierta en foros en línea y páginas wiki en desuso.
PUBLICIDAD
El martes, un investigador de Anthropic anunció públicamente su renuncia y acusó tanto a esa compañía como a OpenAI de actuar de manera irresponsable en el desarrollo de sistemas de IA cada vez más capaces.
Por su parte, el director ejecutivo de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, anunció el sábado que su empresa se compromete a otorgar a evaluadores independientes acceso permanente y con nivel de empleado dentro de la compañía. La iniciativa forma parte de un plan más amplio que, según él, busca frenar el ritmo del desarrollo de la IA. “Debemos reducir el ritmo al que mejoramos las capacidades de los modelos de IA”, escribió en una publicación de blog.
PUBLICIDAD
Un posible pacto entre las principales empresas de IA
Altman sugirió que OpenAI y otras compañías líderes en inteligencia artificial podrían estar cerca de anunciar un acuerdo para frenar el desarrollo de la IA y abordar de manera colectiva los riesgos de seguridad que aumentan con rapidez. Según informó Bloomberg, en una reunión con empleados de OpenAI a principios de esta semana, el directivo señaló que la compañía evaluaba frenar el avance de su tecnología de inteligencia artificial más avanzada.
El viernes, Altman le dijo a Fortune que está dispuesto a postergar la IPO de OpenAI con tal de cumplir con lo que la seguridad requiere, y explicó que “la sociedad necesita lidiar con estos modelos en cada nivel de capacidad”. También mencionó que la compañía discutió la posibilidad de pausas a medida que se alcanzan nuevos niveles de capacidad, para permitir avances adicionales en seguridad y alineación.
PUBLICIDAD
Según Altman, la industria de la inteligencia artificial en su conjunto, y de manera ideal los gobiernos extranjeros, deberían unirse en torno a este asunto.
Altman también hizo referencia a la particular estructura de gobernanza de OpenAI, dividida entre entidades sin fines de lucro y con fines de lucro. “Hemos tolerado esta estructura increíblemente compleja durante mucho tiempo, y este momento en el que estamos ahora es en parte la razón”, expresó. “Necesitamos poder tomar decisiones que no benefician de manera evidente a nuestro negocio ni a nuestros accionistas, en virtud de la responsabilidad de cumplir nuestra misión y lo que eso va a requerir”.

articles.title: Hyderabad houses 515 GCCs, to add 50-70 in next 1 year: report
articles.text:
Hyderabad houses 515 GCCs, to add 50-70 in next 1 year: report
Hyderabad accounts for around 20% of total GCCs in India
Hyderabad has around 515 Global Capability Centres (GCCs), and 50-70 more will be set up within a year, as the city offers a huge talent pool and cost advantage to foreign companies, according to a FICCI and Anarock report.
Industry body FICCI and property consultant Anarock have come up with a joint report titled 'Hyderabad: The Rise of a Global Capability Powerhouse'.
The report highlighted that there were around 515 GCCs in Hyderabad as of March 2026, employing more than 3 lakh people. Hyderabad accounts for around 20% of the total GCCs in India, transforming the city from a cyber city to the GCC hub.
The report noted that GCCs have become a key demand driver for Hyderabad's office market. The leasing of office space by foreign firms to set up GCCs rose to 4.5 million sq ft in 2025 from 1.9 million sq ft in 2021. In the first six months of this year, the number has crossed 3 million sq ft.
"The sustained leasing momentum reflects the deepening of Hyderabad's GCC ecosystem and the increasing preference of global enterprises to establish larger and more sophisticated operations in the city," Anarock Chairman Anuj Puri said.
Hyderabad's GCC proposition is broadening well beyond conventional IT-ITeS functions, said V V Rama Raju, Chairman, FICCI Telangana State Council.
The city's proposition is broadening beyond traditional IT-ITeS into a multi-sector ecosystem, including BFSI, life sciences, semiconductors, engineering and healthcare.
Besides having a huge talent pool, Hyderabad's prime office rent at Rs 95-115 per square ft is lower than Bengaluru and competitive to Pune.
On the future potential, the report said that 50-70 additional GCCs across technology, engineering, BFSI, life sciences, analytics, consulting and digital operations are expected to come within a year.
Sattva Group and Blackstone-sponsored Knowledge Realty Trust CEO Shirish Godbole said, "The GCC boom reinforces Hyderabad's position as one of India's most important office markets for the next decade."

articles.title: Tesla va enfin montrer le Roadster avec ses propulseurs pour décoller du sol, la date de présentation est officielle
articles.text:
Tesla va enfin montrer le Roadster avec ses propulseurs pour décoller du sol, la date de présentation est officielle
Ça y est. Après des années d’attente et de promesses, Tesla nous donne enfin rendez-vous pour dévoiler son nouveau Roadster. Une date de présentation a même été officialisée pour cette supercar électrique qui promet de décoller du sol.
C’est le vendredi 2 octobre 2026 à 2h30 du matin, heure de Paris, que Tesla présentera le nouveau Roadster à Waco au Texas. Une image inédite a été partagée par le constructeur sur X et laisse entendre qu’il y aura une démonstration des fameux propulseurs développés avec SpaceX. Rappelons que depuis des années, Elon Musk nous promet que cette technologie permettra à la supercar électrique de quitter brièvement le sol pendant sa course.
Rendez-vous le 2 octobre pour découvrir le Roadster
— Tesla (@Tesla) September 12, 2026
L’image s’accompagne aussi du message “Go for launch”, soit “Prêt pour le lancement” dans la langue de Molière. Le visuel partagé rappelle beaucoup le décollage d’une fusée, d’où cette théorie sur le fait que les propulseurs seront très importants lors de cette présentation. D’autant plus que Waco se trouve près du site de SpaceX de McGregor où l’entreprise teste ses moteurs de fusée. Bref, le choix du Texas colle parfaitement au projet.
Avec un nouveau Roadster qu’Elon Musk nous promet équipé de propulseurs à gaz froid depuis très longtemps. Ce principe repose sur des réservoirs qui expulsent du gaz à haute pression par plusieurs buses. La poussée en plus permet alors à la supercar d’accélérer encore plus fort et de décoller brièvement.
Mais rappelons que Tesla ne nous a encore jamais montré une version de production capable d’effectuer ce petit vol. Et des informations récentes nous parlent d’une démonstration beaucoup plus encadrée que prévu lors de l'événement. Le Roadster équipé des propulseurs serait contrôlé à distance sans personne dans l’habitacle.
Le public serait aussi à plusieurs centaines de mètres car le bruit de cette technologie pourrait endommager l’audition et cette version spéciale ne serait pas homologuée pour circuler sur la route. Bien évidemment, ce ne sont que des informations qui n’ont pas été confirmées par Tesla et qui restent donc à prendre avec des pincettes.
Une supercar électrique attendue depuis 9 ans
Le Roadster est attendu depuis longtemps. C’est en novembre 2017 que Tesla a dévoilé le premier prototype de cette nouvelle génération. L’entreprise promettait un passage de 0 à 100 km/h en 2,1 secondes, plus de 400 km/h et environ 1 000 km d’autonomie. Puis une production fut annoncée en 2020, mais rien du tout.
En novembre 2025, Elon Musk a parlé d’une démonstration pour le 1er avril 2026. Il a même plaisanté à propos de cette date en expliquant qu’elle lui servirait d’échappatoire en prétextant un poisson d’avril. Et le 1er avril, justement, la présentation n’a pas eu lieu. Et rebelote en juin 2026, le projet a été reporté en août.
Mais désormais, avec ce visuel, il semblerait que tout soit prêt pour la présentation d’octobre 2026 au Texas. Les premiers clients attendent quand même depuis près de neuf ans. Parmi les plus célèbres, Sam Altman lui-même, créateur de ChatGPT, qui a demandé le remboursement de sa réservation après plus de sept ans d’attente
En 2017, Tesla demandait quand même 50 000 $ pour réserver le Roadster dans sa version de base et 250 000 $ pour la Founders Series. Tesla jouera donc gros avec cette présentation du nouveau Roadster qui nous montrera jusqu’où l’entreprise est allée avec SpaceX pour ces fameux propulseurs.
Aura-t-on une date de disponibilité pour la version de série ou encore un prix définitif ? Les clients qui ont réservé en alignant de grosses sommes verront-ils enfin leur commande honorée ? Réponse dans quelques semaines.

articles.title: TechCrunch Mobility: Lyft has entered the robotaxi chat | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation, and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility!
Lyft reached a new milestone this week when Waymo robotaxis landed on its app in Nashville. Under the partnership, Lyft handles fleet services, such as vehicle readiness and maintenance, as well as infrastructure and depot operations through its wholly owned subsidiary Flexdrive.
In Nashville, customers can hail a Waymo robotaxi directly from the Waymo app, or try their luck on the Lyft app, which will match riders with a Waymo depending on availability.
Lyft has more than dabbled in autonomous vehicle technology over the years, including through partnerships with Aptiv (now Motional) in Las Vegas, May Mobility in Atlanta, Baidu in London, and Waymo in Phoenix. But this week is notable because it marks Lyft’s first true entry into commercial robotaxi services using driverless vehicles without a human operator behind the wheel.
Lest you forget, the company spent four years and millions of dollars developing its own AV tech under its Level 5 business division. Lyft sold its autonomous vehicle unit to Toyota’s Woven Planet Holdings subsidiary for $550 million in 2021 — one of many acquisitions during a period of widespread consolidation across the nascent industry.
Lyft then took a break from AVs as it focused on its core ride-hailing business. But it didn’t dismiss the idea altogether.
I spoke to Jeremy Bird, Lyft’s executive vice president of growth, about the milestone and thought I would share a few insights. In his role, Bird manages Lyft’s international, luxury, and autonomous vehicle plans — and sometimes all three may converge.
When I asked Bird when we’ll see more robotaxis on the Lyft app — and where — he didn’t get too specific. But he did say the company went into 2026 focused on its partnership with Waymo in Nashville and Baidu in London (where commercial service has not yet launched).
“I think next year what you’ll see is more diversification of that,” he said, adding that ideally this would include expanding Lyft’s partnership with both partners. “I think next year will be a big year for us.”
And it seems international markets are a big part of that AV expansion plan. Bird called London a “fascinating market,” and throughout our conversation he repeatedly talked about Lyft as a global company, a notable shift from just a few years ago when it was focused on the U.S. market.
So, where is Lyft headed next? When it comes to international markets, Lyft seems to be prioritizing locations where it can operate a hybrid network — meaning AVs and human-driven vehicles — from the get-go.
“We are a global company becoming more global, which is important for us,” he said. “And AVs will be the way we think about the future. Like any market we go into, is there an AV component to that? Is it a market where AVs are already open regulatorily, or that would put that market up higher on our list of the places we want to go?”
A little bird
A little bird noticed a couple of interesting hires over at Ford that sure look like the company is building up its defense tech muscles. Ford recently hired ex-Raytheon employee Tomaz Seignemartin as VP of continuous improvement and former General Dynamics staffer Shirish Srinivasan, who is now chief of staff to Ford’s chief strategy officer. Ford also hired Nathan Rigoni, who was Lockheed Martin’s generative AI team lead, as senior software engineer.
Now, of course, a handful of defense tech hires at a company that employs thousands is hardly a trend. But it does illustrate how having a background in defense tech has become more valuable.
Got a tip for us? Email Kirsten Korosec at kirsten.korosec@techcrunch.com or my Signal at kkorosec.07, or email Sean O’Kane at sean.okane@techcrunch.com.
Deals!
The Boring Company, the startup founded by Elon Musk to “solve traffic” by creating a network of underground tunnels, raised $3 billion in a round led by the United Arab Emirates. The Boring Company is now valued at $23 billion, the company shared in its announcement. There is a reason for UAE’s support. The Boring Company, which already worked with the UAE on the Dubai Loop, said it will dig another 150 kilometers of tunnels in the Middle Eastern country.
Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia Capital, Human Capital, Vy Capital, and Valor Equity Partners also participated.
In the U.S., the Boring Company’s most visible work is in Las Vegas, where it has developed tunnels connecting hotel casinos such as Resorts World, Encore, and the Sahara, the convention center, and limited trips to the airport. Tesla vehicles, driven by a human, shuttle riders to and from these locations.
Other deals that got my attention this week …
ARC Ride, the Kenya-based electric mobility startup, raised $33.3 million in a round led by Novastar Ventures and Norrsken22. Other backers included IFC, British International Investment, Proparco, Japanese supplier Musashi Seimitsu, and African impact investor Talanton.
Beep, a startup known for operating autonomous shuttles at campuses and airports, raised $20 million in a Series B round led by Mobileye, one of its existing tech partners. The Orlando, Florida-based company that was founded in 2019 said it has raised $130 million to date.
Fryte Mobility, a Munich, Germany-based software startup focused on charging logistics for electric trucks, raised €3.5 million ($4 million) in seed funding co-led by 4impact capital and Rethink Ventures. Existing backers Revent, F-LOG, accilium ventures, and unnamed angel investors also participated.
Porsche completed the sale of its stakes in Bugatti Rimac and Rimac Group to HOF Capital. Porsche received about 1 billion euros in the sale, and about 250 million euros of those proceeds will be used to further fund its pension obligations.
Poseidon Aerospace raised $60 million ahead of the first test flight of its uncrewed cargo plane, Egret, expected by the end of this year. The Series A round was led by early-stage VC firm TQ Ventures and saw new investments from Hanwha Asset Management, G Squared, and JAWS. Existing backers Starship Ventures, Draper Associates, and Drover Ventures also invested.
Stoke Space may not be a traditional transportation player, but the reusable rocket company’s $1 billion raise, and some of its backers, got my attention. The round was led by Point72 Ventures (hedge fund billionaire Steve Cohen’s tech investment vehicle) and Spark Capital, and included investment from General Innovation, Glade Brook Capital, US Innovative Technology, Washington Harbour Partners, Woven Capital, and Y Combinator, among others.
Tern, the Austin, Texas-based startup developing an alternative to GPS, landed an $11.26 million contract from the U.S. Army. The startup said U.S. Army vehicles will use its “Google Maps for the battlefield” tech.
Uber invested $10 million in Indian fleet management startup Carrum Mobility in a Series B round. The new investment values Carrum at ₹16 billion (about $168 million) post-money.
Notable reads and other tidbits
Autonomy, the California electric vehicle subscription service created by TrueCar founder Scott Painter, is pivoting. The company, which almost went out of business, is adding internal combustion engine vehicles to its fleet.
Beta Technologies, Joby Aviation, and Wisk, three companies developing electric aircraft, began test flight demonstrations in Texas as part of the Federal Aviation Administration’s Advanced Air Mobility and Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) Integration Pilot Program (eIPP). The weeklong campaign will allow these companies to test real-world routes, including to the Dallas-Fort Worth Airport.
Travis Kalanick’s startup Atoms is preparing for a hiring spree in a bid to go after the robotaxi business, the Financial Times reported.
TechCrunch reporter Jagmeet Singh digs into Uber rival inDrive and its push to scale beyond ride-hailing.
One more thing …
U.S.-based autonomous vehicle developers may get the bulk of the attention these days, but there is a lot of notable activity occurring outside of the country. This week alone we saw China AV developer Pony.ai and Croatia-based Verne (another Mate Rimac company) begin fully driverless test rides with passengers on public roads in Zagreb, while Spain issued the first national AV permits to WeRide and partners Uber and Avomo.
Meanwhile, Chinese autonomous delivery company Neolix began testing on a closed course in Japan, and Pony.ai pulled the human safety operator out of its AV test vehicles during demonstrations in Doha, Qatar. Pony.ai, along with partner Mowasalat, still has human operators behind the wheel of robotaxis in its commercial service.

articles.title: Chinese military researchers and tech giants caught using Claude — US frontier model coded 16 air-defense suppression tools targeting Taiwan, drafted anti-torpedo specs, and fed 151 million training queries to Alibaba
articles.text:
Chinese military researchers and tech giants caught using Claude — US frontier model coded 16 air-defense suppression tools targeting Taiwan, drafted anti-torpedo specs, and fed 151 million training queries to Alibaba
Is imitation the sincerest form of flattery?
While China claims to have advanced AI models that may well compete against those developed in the U.S., for some reason, hundreds of China-linked agents allegedly used Anthropic for at least five different programs: two military, two surveillance, and one aimed at distilling Claude's capabilities, according to Anthropic's September 2026 threat report.
Two military programs
One China-based actor used Claude to draft a fire-control specification for an anti-torpedo fire-control system (the core logic that determines when and where an anti-torpedo weapon should engage an incoming threat), test the potential system against U.S. Navy anti-torpedo and anti-submarine systems based on public knowledge about these programs, and prep a 200+ page technical proposal for a potential client. While the actor disguised itself as an OEM in the U.S. defense sector, Anthropic believes that the actor was associated with a Chinese defense manufacturer seeking to develop a system for the People's Liberation Army Navy.
Another China-based defense and military-industrial researcher used Claude to develop about 16 software modules for electronic warfare and suppression of enemy air defenses. The software analyzed radars, SAM sites, command posts, and communications nodes and prioritized targets. At one point, the default scenario contained 12 targets in Taiwan, including Patriot and Tien Kung batteries, air bases, an early-warning radar, and a command bunker. Interestingly, Anthropic claims that account metadata and content caught by its safeguards 'indicated the actor was linked to PRC research institutions, including the PLA Academy of Military Sciences,' though it does not outright say that Claude was used by the PLA.
Given China's considerable AI capabilities — which may still lag behind those of the United States in some areas (more on this later) — it is striking that two Chinese military-related projects relied on Anthropic's Claude. Given the Chinese-language prompts and other account-level evidence identified by Anthropic, plausible deniability hardly seems to have been the primary reason for choosing Claude over domestic alternatives. More likely, Claude was simply better or more convenient for these particular engineering workflows, particularly coding, reasoning, and agentic tasks. There may also have been another advantage: U.S. frontier models are trained on enormous amounts of English-language material and could therefore have particularly extensive knowledge of publicly available information about American military technologies and systems.
Given China's major AI prowess (which may well fall short of American, but still be quite capable), it is interesting to see two Chinese military projects using Anthropic AI. Given Chinese IP addresses and Chinese language prompts detected by Anthropic, plausible deniability is certainly not the main reason for using Claude instead of using domestic tools (more on this later). Apparently, Claude was better or more convenient for these particular engineering workflows (coding => reasoning => agentic) than whatever models the actors could readily access. Furthermore, after all, U.S. frontier models were trained mostly on English-language materials, and they may have way more information about American military capability than Chinese spy channels have ever gotten (we are speculating, of course).
Significant surveillance activities
Anthropic also disrupted China-linked surveillance operations related to Uyghurs outside of China, perhaps because similar operations are already in place in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. One China government-linked actor used Claude to infiltrate Uyghur armed groups in Syria and surveil Uyghur diaspora activists and media, while posing as an Arabic-speaking 'expert' consultant.
Once the agent had infiltrated the said groups, Claude helped process information collected from more than a hundred WhatsApp groups and dozens of Telegram channels, identify people across platforms, map social networks, and reveal potential recruitment targets considered vulnerable because of financial problems, family separation, or ideological disillusionment with the new Syrian government.
The actor also singled out individuals with relatives remaining in Xinjiang, while Claude helped draft deceptive approaches in local dialects, locate people and organizations, translate conversations in real time, and evaluate the credibility of recruitment messages. The same operation targeted diaspora journalists, particularly Uyghur Post, with coordinated mass-reporting and bot-amplification campaigns.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Stealing from Anthropic
Perhaps the most ironic thing about Anthropic's findings is that Chinese entities steal from the company. While reported broadly in 2024 – 2025, it does not stop Chinese entities from using distillation, the main way to 'steal' an AI model's capabilities without obtaining the model itself.
Anthropic says several major Chinese AI developers conducted industrial-scale distillation campaigns designed to extract Claude's reasoning and other capabilities and reproduce them in their own models. The largest one allegedly came from Alibaba, whose operators generated more than 151 million Claude exchanges between May and July 2026. At one point, this approached 3 million requests per day through thousands of fraudulent accounts. Anthropic says the harvested chain-of-thought data helped train Qwen 3.x, particularly for reasoning, coding, agentic software engineering, kernel development, and long-horizon tasks, according to Anthropic.
Alibaba is far from alone, as Anthropic accuses DeepSeek, Xiaomi, Zhipu/Z.ai, and others of similar campaigns. Techniques they have allegedly used span from proxy networks and fraudulent accounts to disguising the secret entity all the way to forwarding their own customers' requests to Claude and purchasing harvested Claude conversations from third parties. DeepSeek alone allegedly generated more than 12.1 million exchanges in 14 days, while Xiaomi generated more than 400,000.
Anthropic defines this activity as distillation: covertly extracting a frontier model's answers and then replicating the knowledge at a fraction of the compute, time, and cost required to develop them in-house.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Tomar el café o el té demasiado caliente puede triplicar el riesgo de cáncer de esófago. La clave está en la temperatura
articles.text:
A día de hoy, el aumento en la preocupación por nuestra salud ha hecho que poco a poco sepamos mucho más sobre aquellos elementos de nuestra vida cotidiana que nos pueden generar una enfermedad como el cáncer. Y aquí las bebidas calientes pueden tener un papel muy importante, puesto que un reciente artículo publicado en The Guardian apunta a que tomar café o té calientes triplica el riesgo de sufrir cáncer de esófago.
Su origen. Llegar a esta conclusión es el resultado de una investigación realizada por la Universidad de Oxford, aunque por suerte no significa que con tomar de manera aislada un líquido demasiado caliente automáticamente se produzca un cáncer. Y es que, como ocurre en muchas ocasiones, hace falta una exposición prolongada para que se dé este desenlace.
El calor. Para entender el debate, hay que remontarse a 2016. Ese año, la Agencia Internacional para la Investigación del Cáncer (IARC), dependiente de la OMS, evaluó el consumo de café, mate y bebidas calientes. Su conclusión apuntó a que las bebidas consumidas por encima de los 65 ºC se clasifican como "probablemente carcinógenas para los humanos", específicamente por su relación con el cáncer de esófago.
La IARC en este caso dejó bastante claro que esta categorización se refería exclusivamente al daño térmico, o lo que es lo mismo, sufrir quemaduras microscópicas y repetidas en el tejido del esófago día tras día. Y aquí un estudio ya encontró poca evidencia de que la cantidad de café o té consumida por sí sola aumentara el riesgo de cáncer, pero sí observó que las temperaturas más elevadas estaban estrechamente relacionadas con una mayor incidencia de la enfermedad.
Lo más reciente. El pilar principal de estas afirmaciones se apoya en estudios masivos como el relacionado con el UK Biobank, donde se analizó a 454.796 adultos durante una media de más de 11 años. Aquí los resultados vieron que, en comparación con quienes tomaban sus bebidas "templadas", aquellos que las describían como "muy calientes" tenían un riesgo 2,5 veces mayor de desarrollar carcinoma escamoso de esófago.
Este patrón se repite en otras partes del mundo, puesto que un estudio de casos y controles realizado en Kenia encontró que quienes consumían bebidas "muy calientes" presentaban un riesgo 3,7 veces mayor frente a los que las tomaban templadas, reforzando la hipótesis de la lesión térmica continuada.
Triplicar el riesgo. Cuando hablamos de que la bebida caliente supone un gran riesgo para nuestro esófago, parece que nuestras probabilidades de enfermedad son inmensas. Pero en epidemiología, esto es un riesgo relativo, no un riesgo absoluto.
Aquí hay que saber que el cáncer de esófago, y en particular el carcinoma escamoso, es una enfermedad relativamente infrecuente en la población general de países occidentales. Para ponerlo en perspectiva, en el gigantesco estudio del UK Biobank, de los más de 454.000 participantes seguidos durante una década, solo se identificaron 242 casos de carcinoma escamoso. De esta manera, triplicar un riesgo basal que de por sí es minúsculo significa que el riesgo absoluto para la inmensa mayoría de las personas sigue siendo extremadamente bajo.

articles.title: BlockChance Offers 1,000 KH/s Solo Mining Without a Dedicated PC for Just $50 Through Today
articles.text:
Sunday, September 13th 2026
	
	
	
	
BlockChance Offers 1,000 KH/s Solo Mining Without a Dedicated PC for Just $50 Through Today
Bitcoin mining typically brings to mind specialized hardware, substantial power consumption, and large mining operations. The BlockChance Bitcoin Ticket Miner, available for $49.97 (MSRP $149.99) through Sept. 10, takes a much smaller and more probability-driven approach.
BlockChance is a standalone solo-mining device that generates what the company describes as mining "lottery tickets." Instead of steadily earning small fractions of Bitcoin, the objective is to successfully mine a full Bitcoin block. The tradeoff is important: the probability of doing so is extremely low.
The device provides a 1,000 KH/s hashrate, which the manufacturer says is about 18 times higher than typical ticket miners. Its stated estimated probability is approximately one in 930 million per block, one in 6.5 million per day, and one in 17,800 annually, or roughly 0.0056%. Actual results can change with Bitcoin network difficulty and hashrate fluctuations.
Get this BlockChance Desktop Bitcoin Miner for just $49.97 (MSRP $149.99) through Sept. 10 only.BlockChance runs official, license-free NMMiner firmware and doesn't require a connected computer. After connecting it to Wi-Fi, the 2.8-inch touchscreen displays information including hashrate, ticket submissions, mining pool details, and real-time probability statistics.
The ESP32-based hardware supports Wi-Fi and BLE connectivity, along with over-the-air updates. Free lifetime firmware upgrades are also included. According to the manufacturer, the device operates silently and consumes less electricity than a light bulb.
This isn't hardware to buy with an expectation of reliably earning Bitcoin. Its appeal is instead as a compact, low-power way for Bitcoin enthusiasts and tinkerers to experiment with solo mining—and understand just how improbable successfully mining a block can be.

articles.title: PlayStation cancela juego de Hide Kojima, pero Xbox rescata el proyecto
articles.text:
Hideo Kojima, el diseñador japonés detrás de la saga Metal Gear, anunció en redes sociales la cancelación de Physint por parte de Sony y el traspaso inmediato del desarrollo a Xbox. El título, concebido como un sucesor espiritual de Metal Gear dentro del género de acción y espionaje, había sido presentado a principios de 2024 como un proyecto en fase temprana, respaldado por casi tres décadas de colaboración entre Kojima y PlayStation.
La ruptura se formalizó en junio, cuando PlayStation Studios envió una comunicación a Kojima Productions en la que informaba su decisión de apartarse del proyecto. “Tras una cuidadosa consideración, hemos tomado la difícil decisión de apartarnos de la colaboración con Kojima Productions en su proyecto Physint”, señaló la compañía, que aclaró que la relación con el estudio “sigue siendo sólida”.
PUBLICIDAD
Las razones detrás de la decisión de Sony
De acuerdo con fuentes consultadas por el periodista Jason Schreier en un artículo de Bloomberg, la cancelación respondió a preocupaciones internas por el elevado presupuesto del proyecto y el incumplimiento de plazos de desarrollo. Las mismas fuentes, que pidieron mantenerse en el anonimato, señalaron que Sony también evaluaba la rentabilidad potencial del título y su condición de exclusividad.
Un antecedente pesó en la decisión: Death Stranding y su secuela no alcanzaron las expectativas de ingresos que la compañía había proyectado. A eso se sumó que Physint, sin cumplir los hitos de desarrollo previstos, ya demandaba un presupuesto superior al estimado inicialmente, con años todavía por delante hasta su eventual lanzamiento.
PUBLICIDAD
La cuestión de la exclusividad añadió otra capa al conflicto. Sony mostraba reticencia a invertir cientos de millones de dólares en un juego que no permaneciera de forma permanente en sus consolas. Kojima Productions, que posee la propiedad intelectual de Death Stranding, había lanzado ambas entregas de esa saga como exclusivos temporales de PlayStation, hasta que con el tiempo llegaron a otras plataformas.
Un cambio de filosofía en PlayStation
Según las fuentes citadas por Schreier, PlayStation modificó sus procedimientos internos de aprobación de proyectos tras el fracaso de Concord, uno de los mayores tropiezos de su historia dentro de la estrategia de impulsar juegos como servicio. Ese episodio derivó en una nueva política que aplica plazos de desarrollo más estrictos a las producciones en curso.
PUBLICIDAD
El periodista también constató un cambio en el vínculo personal entre Kojima y la compañía japonesa. La relación se remonta a los tiempos de PS1 con Metal Gear Solid y se mantuvo incluso después de que el creativo abandonara Konami para fundar Kojima Productions. Sin embargo, buena parte de los ejecutivos que sostenían una relación cercana con el diseñador dejaron la empresa en los últimos años.
Xbox asume el desarrollo y suma derechos audiovisuales
Tras conocerse la cancelación, Kojima Productions inició la búsqueda de un nuevo socio para continuar con el desarrollo. “Encontramos que Xbox es el socio con el que podemos compartir una ‘visión de futuro’”, explicó Kojima, en referencia a OD, otro proyecto que ya desarrolla junto a la compañía estadounidense.
PUBLICIDAD
Asha Sharma, CEO de Xbox, respaldó la decisión: “Nos enorgullece que Kojima-san haya elegido Xbox para trabajar con Kojima Productions en Physint. Su ambición y desafío a las convenciones es el tipo de creatividad que queremos apoyar en Xbox”.
El nuevo acuerdo entre ambas compañías incluye derechos de producción para cine y televisión, tanto para Physint como para OD, en línea con la estrategia de Xbox de expandir sus propiedades intelectuales hacia medios lineales.
PUBLICIDAD
Un factor adicional favoreció el acercamiento con la compañía de Redmond: Xbox lanza sus títulos tanto en consola como en PC, un modelo que coincide con la estrategia de distribución que Kojima Productions ya había aplicado con el primer Death Stranding, apoyado por la editora 505 Games para su llegada a computadoras. Sony, en cambio, anunció que no planea lanzar más exclusivos en PC, lo que habría obligado a Kojima Productions a buscar un socio externo para esa plataforma.
“Tened la seguridad de que el desarrollo de Physint, nuestro juego que redefinirá el género de la acción y el espionaje, seguirá adelante”, afirmó Kojima en su comunicado. Por el momento no se conocen las plataformas definitivas ni una ventana de lanzamiento para el título.

articles.title: India's semiconductor sector gets $1.4 billion: report
articles.text:
India's semiconductor sector gets $1.4 billion: report
Nearly half of the funding amount into Indian semiconductor companies was raised since 2025
India's semiconductor sector has attracted $1.4 billion in all-time equity funding across 281 funded companies, with nearly half of this amount - $701 million - raised since 2025 alone, according to data from Tracxn.
The findings come days ahead of SEMICON India 2026, the country's flagship semiconductor conference and exhibition, which will be held from September 17-19 at Yashobhoomi in Dwarka, New Delhi.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the fifth edition of SEMICON India 2026 on September 17, a mega-event set to bring together global semiconductor industry leaders, government officials, state representatives, and sector experts as India builds on the momentum of its growing semiconductor ecosystem.
India is home to 3,557 companies in the sector, of which 142 have raised equity funding, out of 281 funded companies. The sector recorded $228 million in funding in 2026 year-to-date (YTD), according to Tracxn.
Tessolve Semiconductor leads the sector in cumulative funding at $213 million till date, followed by ILJIN Electronics (USD 198 million) and VVDN ($129 million).
Electronic Manufacturing Services has led the sector's funding, securing $313 million since 2025.
Embedded Hardware ranked second, with $51.9 million raised since 2025 — entirely within the trailing 12 months — while Power Management Integrated Circuits and Fabless Semiconductor Manufacturers were among the other leading business models by funding.
According to the report, the sector's funding rose from $49 million in 2021 to $473 million in 2025. The five-year funding compound annual growth rate (CAGR) stood at over 36 per cent.
Bengaluru remained the dominant hub, home to 626 of the sector's 3,557 companies — about 18 per cent of the total — and accounting for 40.1 per cent of all equity funding raised to date. It was followed by Noida (16.4 per cent), Gurugram (10.7 per cent), Kochi (8.8 per cent) and Hyderabad (6.2 per cent) in terms of funding share.

articles.title: El país más rico de la Tierra se está quedando sin agua, literalmente
articles.text:
El río Colorado es la vaca lechera del Norte de América. Tras 2.333 kilómetros de recorrido, atraviesa el suroeste de Estados Unidos y el noroeste de México antes de desembocar en el Pacífico. En su curso por EEUU abastece a siete estados, lo que supone más del 10% de su población. Tras décadas soportando la sequía, este año además ha habido un verano con temperaturas récord y un invierno con nevadas históricamente bajas. ¿El resultado? El 95% de su cuenca está en sequía, como recoge CNN.
En pocas palabras, el río Colorado está bajo mínimos y ha sucedido en el peor momento posible: cuando las normas que regulan el reparto de sus aguas están a punto de caducar.
No hay acuerdo. Las reglas vigentes de repartición expiran a finales de 2026 y mientras tanto, los siete estados que forman el Colorado River Compact no llegaron a un acuerdo para cerrarlo en el plazo previsto (en febrero), como recoge el Colorado Sun. Con este panorama, el gobierno federal impuso este verano su propio marco de gestión. Nevada respondió a este movimiento con una demanda.
No obstante, podría ser peor: dentro de Estados Unidos no hay quórum, pero hace unos días EEUU y Mexico firmaron las reglas de reparto para 2027 y 2028: México reducirá su consumo en unos 308 millones de metros cúbicos al año (más de 100.000 piscinas olímpicas, explica el Colorado Sun) cuando el nivel de los embalses sea bajo. A cambio, gana en flexibilidad para acumular agua hasta fin del plazo. Por su parte, EEUU se compromete a reducir el consumo de agua en 1.542 millones de metros cúbicos al año en los estados de Arizona, California y Nevada y a funcionar como banco de agua para México.
Por qué pasa. Ya hemos visto algunos datos de su acuciante sequía, con sus dos mayores embalses (los lagos Mead y Powell) en mínimos históricos que no se veían desde 1957. Pero hay dos problemas de base más: el destino de ese agua y cómo se gestiona el agua. De todo el agua del río Colorado, el 74% va destinada a la agricultura, como detalla este paper reciente. Y de esta, casi la mitad se va al cultivo de alfalfa y otros forrajes para ganado. Más concretamente, el 47% del agua que se extrae del río acaba alimentando a las vacas.
Un dato: la alfalfa representa un 0,2% del PIB de Utah, pero se lleva el 68% del agua disponible, explica esta columna de opinión del Salt Lake Tribune que invita a dejar el agua correr. ¿Por qué actúa Utah así viendo el percal? En pocas palabras: porque puede, según los antiquísimos derechos del agua del oeste (en el sentido más western de la palabra), que datan de la época de los colonos del siglo XIX. Se rigen por la "apropiación previa": quien llega primero y reclama el agua, tiene preferencia hasta el final de los tiempos.
El conflicto entre estados. Así, mientras que los estados de la cuenca baja del colorado (California, Arizona y Nevada) ya se han comprometido a recortes significativos como los anteriormente mencionados, los de la cuenca alta (Colorado, Utah, Nuevo México y Wyoming) se niegan a asumir reducciones. ¿Los motivos de su no? Cuenta el New York Times que según la cuenca alta, la cuenca baja consume más de lo debido (argumentan que California y Arizona llevan años sobreconsumiendo) y defienden su derecho legal histórico.
Pequeños parches para mientras. Ya hay varias localidades que han empezado a actuar en vista de lo que se les viene encima. Phoenix está promoviendo programas de reciclaje de agua, Las Vegas está quitando jardines para reducir el consumo y en Utah están subiendo las tarifas para quienes más consumen.
Recordemos que uno de los grandes problemas de fondo es el gasto en la agricultura. Pues bien, hay programas para pagar a los agricultores para dejar sus tierras en barbecho e iniciativas para mejorar la eficiencia de riego, como este de California o este otro de Arizona. Casi todas las iniciativas provienen de la cuenca baja, por lo que sea. Aunque estas medidas reducen el consumo de agua, siguen siendo insuficientes frente a la realidad de la cuenca y ese consumo agrícola desmesurado.
¿Qué pasa si no se llega a un acuerdo? Si para fin de año no hay acuerdo, el Departamento de Interior de EEUU ya ha demostrado que está dispuesto a imponer un marco de gestión unilateral como ya ha hecho este verano ante el bloqueo, aunque esto genere tensiones. O que el asunto acabe en los tribunales, pudiendo dilatarse durante décadas, lo que generaría incertidumbre a la ciudadanía, agricultura o las industrias que necesitan el agua del Colorado.
En cualquier caso, que no se llegue a una decisión global en la estrategia de consumo que tenga en cuenta ese complicado equilibrio entre las necesidades de abastecimiento, las actividades y la realidad del cambio climático puede desembocar en que los embalses sigan bajando. Y si eso pasa, ya hay una advertencia sobre la mesa: para 2027 el lago Powell puede dejar de ser capaz de generar electricidad.

articles.title: Carte bancaire ou smartphone : pourquoi le paiement sans contact sur téléphone est (beaucoup) plus sûr que vous ne le pensez
articles.text:
Carte bancaire ou smartphone : pourquoi le paiement sans contact sur téléphone est (beaucoup) plus sûr que vous ne le pensez
Si le paiement sans contact (NFC) fait aujourd'hui partie du quotidien, que ce soit par carte bancaire ou smartphone, la solution mobile peine encore à convaincre l'ensemble des utilisateurs. Elle offre pourtant des avantages indéniables face au traditionnel morceau de plastique. Explications.
Il y aura toujours des irréductibles pour préférer désactiver le NFC et régler leurs achats en insérant physiquement leur carte bancaire, puis en composant leur code PIN. Après tout, malgré des technologies toujours plus sûres, il est toujours possible de tomber face à des pirates très motivés capables de contourner les systèmes, dont le NFC, pour accéder à votre argent. Pourtant, payer sans contact n'a jamais été aussi commode et sécurisé, notamment depuis un smartphone.
Carte bancaire ou smartphone : quelles différences pour le paiement sans contact ?
À première vue, payer via son smartphone plutôt qu'avec sa carte semble accumuler les contraintes. Outre l'obligation de posséder un appareil récent compatible et à jour, il faut prendre la peine de renseigner sa carte bancaire dans une app dédiée (Google Wallet, Samsung Wallet, Apple Cartes…), ce qui donne potentiellement davantage de données personnelles à de grands groupes technologiques.
Cela peut aussi sembler redondant avec l'usage de la carte physique, sans compter que de nombreuses personnes répugnent à centraliser tous leurs usages sur un même téléphone. Perdre ce dernier, où sont parfois réunis cartes bancaires et papiers d'identité, peut rapidement virer au cauchemar (bien que le constat soit similaire avec un portefeuille physique). Même constat en cas de vol ou de batterie qui lâche.
Pourtant, perdre ou se faire voler sa carte bancaire présente aussi un risque réel pour son compte en banque, d'autant que celle-ci n'est pas protégée par la biométrie ou le schéma de verrouillage de votre smartphone. Si un voleur ne peut pas retirer d'argent au distributeur sans votre code PIN, il peut déjà régler des achats sans contact (si l'option est activée) et effectuer des opérations en ligne grâce aux identifiants inscrits au dos de la carte. Un problème que ne connaît pas la version dématérialisée sur smartphone.
Sécurité et plafonds : pourquoi le paiement par smartphone surpasse la carte bancaire
Lors d'un paiement sans contact, là où une carte bancaire transmet son numéro au terminal avec le risque théorique d'être intercepté ou stocké, un paiement par smartphone génère à chaque transaction un jeton chiffré (token) unique et inutilisable pour une personne malintentionnée.
Autre gage de sécurité pour la solution mobile : l'appareil vous demande quasi systématiquement de confirmer votre identité avant de valider le règlement, le plus souvent via une méthode biométrique (empreinte digitale ou reconnaissance faciale). Ainsi, une personne qui récupère votre téléphone ne peut pas payer librement avec, contrairement à ce qu’il se passe avec une carte bancaire.
Enfin, si le côté purement passif et instantané de la carte physique conserve ses adeptes, cette dernière reste soumise à un plafond de paiement sans contact inférieur (50 €) à celui du smartphone, lui limité uniquement par le plafond hebdomadaire/mensuel défini par la banque. Grâce à sa meilleure sécurisation et à l'authentification systématique de l'utilisateur, le paiement sans contact par téléphone permet de régler des montants bien plus importants.
Loin de nous l'idée de vous inciter à choisir une solution plus qu'une autre, mais connaître ces différences permet d'arbitrer en toute connaissance de cause selon vos usages.

articles.title: StarCraft Returns as an Open-World Shooter, Set for 2030
articles.text:
Sunday, September 13th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
StarCraft Returns as an Open-World Shooter, Set for 2030
Blizzard has confirmed a new StarCraft game during the BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony, thus ending a wait that stretched back to StarCraft II's last expansion in 2015. The game is simply called StarCraft, not StarCraft III, and it drops the series' real-time strategy roots entirely, pivoting to an open-world, story-driven shooter. It's set in the Koprulu Sector roughly 70 years after the events of Legacy of the Void, with Blizzard describing it as a fresh story. The project is led by Dan Hay, previously creative director on several Far Cry games at Ubisoft. During the reveal, Hay said the game would be fought "not from above, but down in the mud, in the fire," which signals clear changes in gameplay mechanics. 
The announcement trailer leaned entirely on cinematics, showing Dominion soldiers training and eventually fighting the Zerg, with no gameplay footage shown yet. A 2030 release is a long way off, and Blizzard has been upfront that the game is still early in development. That gives the studio plenty of room to reveal actual gameplay before launch, though it also means specifics on combat systems, world structure, or platforms are still unknown. Given how quiet the franchise has been since 2016's Nova Covert Ops, it's honestly a bit of a surprise Blizzard chose to reinvent StarCraft as a shooter rather than return to its RTS format, though I suspect that's exactly why it's getting attention now.

articles.title: Mexican cartel's crypto farm seized in mountain raid — 300 GPUs, satellite links, and industrial transformers tapped hydroelectric power
articles.text:
Mexican cartel's crypto farm seized in mountain raid — 300 GPUs, satellite links, and industrial transformers tapped hydroelectric power
Police raided a facility in Puebla's mountains and found 300 GPUs, electrical infrastructure, and satellite equipment.
There is increasing evidence that Mexican drug cartels are diversifying into cryptocurrency mining and are using crypto platforms to diversify their income and, at the same time, launder their ill-gotten gains and fund other illegal activities. Reuters reports that local Mexican police uncovered a clandestine cryptocurrency farm in Tlaola, a town located in the leafy mountains of Puebla's Sierra Norte region. They found 300 GPUs, electricity infrastructure, and satellite equipment. The electricity-hungry operation likely drew power by secretly tapping into the grid at Presa de Necaxa, a nearby hydroelectric dam.
While this latest hidden facility found by police may seem small, Reuters notes it is the fourth such crypto farm Mexican authorities have uncovered in this region since early last year. According to a Mexico-based security analyst, the crypto farms discovered show that the cartels are increasingly sophisticated in their operations. In the latest bust, the Mexican federal authorities, the Navy, and state police seized around 300 GPUs, 80 medium-voltage terminations, a transformer, and eight satellite antennas.
It might not be surprising to hear about the Mexican cartels being tied up in crypto. Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, as cited by Reuters, reckons illicit crypto transactions grew from $59 billion in 2024 to $154 billion last year. The firm links the surge recorded to sanctions evasion involving governments. However, in South America, cartels are increasingly interested in using this channel to launder money. The mining operations are also integrated into the scheme, as stealing electricity is easy for organized crime. Mainstream consumer GPU mining ended in H2 2022, flooding the market with used graphics cards.
The source report doesn’t say how authorities found the crypto farm. Perhaps locals in this remote area of Puebla alerted authorities to the operation. Two folks from neighboring communities told Reuters that they could hear the crypto farm noise (transformers, cooling) from a kilometer away (0.6 miles), and the place was apparently a mere 2 km (1.2 miles) from the nearest village. The other three recently uncovered crypto farms were also near the same HEP dam, it is noted. Tlaola is a small community with around 20,000 inhabitants, so the noise levels and power consumption of crypto farms are very perceptible even if the cartels try to hide them deep in the mountains.
Remote communities, such as Tlaola, are popular locations for clandestine crypto farms because the electricity is cheap and most of them are under the protection of the cartels. For example, the Cartel Jalisco Nueva Generación (CJNG) and its armed branch, La Barredora, have the strongest presence in Puebla.
According to SILIKN, a Mexican cybersecurity firm, the use of cryptomining to launder illegal money rose by at least 55.8% last year in México. Drug cartels such as the Cartel de Sinaloa and the CJNG have set up crypto farms to mine Bitcoin (BTC), Monero (XMR), and Tether (USDT).
Similarly remote, illicit cryptomining facilities exist around the world, with Reuters recalling news of raids in Brazil, the U.S., and Thailand. Do you think there’s one near you? Please call the local police and liberate those stressed GPUs. Meanwhile, analysts expect crypto-related crime will reach new heights in the coming years.
